Normalize Cost Columns

Source: R/utils_normalize_data.R
normalize_cost_columns.Rd

Scales cost-related columns to ensure that the maximum value has at most six whole number digits.

Usage

normalize_cost_columns(x, col_starts_with = "Cost")

Arguments

x

A tibble containing raw planning unit data.

col_starts_with

A character string indicating the prefix for cost-related columns. Default is "Cost".

Value

A tibble with normalized cost columns, or NULL if no scaling is required.

Details

This function checks the highest cost value across all columns starting with col_starts_with. If the maximum cost is 1,000,000 or greater, it determines the number of whole number digits and calculates a divisor to scale the values down to six digits. The function returns a modified tibble with the cost columns normalized. If no scaling is needed, it returns NULL.

Examples

library(dplyr)

# Example tibble
df <- tibble(
  ID = 1:3,
  CostA = c(1e7, 500000, 2000000),  # Large values to test normalization
  CostB = c(2500, 999999, 12345678),
  Value = c(10, 20, 30)
)

# Normalize cost columns
normalize_cost_columns(df)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>      ID  CostA   CostB Value
#>   <int>  <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1 100000     25     10
#> 2     2   5000  10000.    20
#> 3     3  20000 123457.    30
